headings.title: Definition of autocycle and federal safety compliance
headings.reviewNote: Defines autocycle as a three-wheeled motor vehicle with partially or completely enclosed nonstraddle seating controlled by steering wheel and pedals meeting applicable NHTSA or Federal Motorcycle Safety Standards.

headings.title: Exemption from protective headgear requirements for autocycles
headings.reviewNote: Provides that notwithstanding section 302.020(2), a person operating or riding in an autocycle may not be required to wear protective headgear.

headings.title: Driver's license required without motorcycle endorsement
headings.reviewNote: Requires a valid driver's license to operate an autocycle on any highway or street while exempting operators from obtaining a motorcycle or motortricycle license or endorsement under sections 302.010 to 302.340.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 304.005 defining autocycles, exempting operators and riders from protective headgear requirements, and requiring a valid driver's license without motorcycle endorsement.

headings.title: Infraction classification for speeding five mph or less over limit
headings.reviewNote: Classifies a section 304.010 speeding violation of five miles per hour or less over the posted speed limit as an infraction with the same court costs as section 304.010.

headings.title: No driver's license points assessed for five mph or less over
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits assessing points under section 302.302 for any speeding violation over the posted speed limit by five miles per hour or less.

headings.title: Court authority to issue failure-to-appear warrant for infraction
headings.reviewNote: Permits a court to issue a warrant for failure to appear for any violation classified as an infraction.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 304.009 classifying speeding five miles per hour or less over the posted limit as an infraction with no points and authorizing failure-to-appear warrants.

headings.title: Definitions of expressway, freeway, rural interstate, and urban area
headings.reviewNote: Defines expressway, freeway, rural interstate, and urbanized area for purposes of section 304.010.

headings.title: Uniform maximum speed limits and posted-limit presumption
headings.reviewNote: Sets uniform maximum speed limits (75 mph rural interstates/freeways, 65 mph rural expressways, 60 mph urbanized and other non-lettered roads, 55 mph lettered roads unless raised to 60 by MoDOT) and creates a rebuttable presumption that the posted limit is legal.

headings.title: Commission authority to raise or lower state highway speed limits
headings.reviewNote: Permits the highways and transportation commission to set higher or lower limits on state highways upon MoDOT recommendation (capped at 75 mph) and allows DPS requests.

headings.title: Municipal speed ordinances on state roads and revenue-only voidance
headings.reviewNote: Permits cities, towns, and villages to regulate speed on state roads within corporate limits with commission approval, and allows the commission to void ordinances not primarily designed to expedite traffic flow and primarily designed to produce revenue.

headings.title: County commission lower speed and weight limits in certain counties
headings.reviewNote: Permits second, third, and fourth classification county commissions to set lower speed limits (max 55 mph posted, 50 mph unposted) and weight limits on county/township/road district roads and, with commission approval, unincorporated state roads.

headings.title: Countywide unincorporated speed limits and nonresident boundary signs
headings.reviewNote: Permits second, third, and fourth classification county commissions to set countywide unincorporated speed limits by ordinance, requiring specified boundary signs to convict nonresidents present forty-eight hours or less.

headings.title: Uniform MoDOT standards for speed and weight limit signs
headings.reviewNote: Requires all road signs indicating speed limits or weight limits to be uniform in size, shape, lettering, and coloring and conform to department of transportation standards.

headings.title: Preservation of pre-March 13, 1996 local limits below fifty-five mph
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section does not alter any speed limit set below fifty-five miles per hour by county or municipal ordinance adopted before March 13, 1996.

headings.title: Exemption for emergency vehicles under section 304.022
headings.reviewNote: Exempts the operation of any emergency vehicle as defined in section 304.022 from the speed limits established under this section.

headings.title: Burden of proving negligence in civil actions unaffected
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that a violation of this section does not relieve parties in civil actions from proving negligence or contributory negligence as proximate cause or defense.

headings.title: Class C and class B misdemeanor penalties for speeding
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violating this section as a class C misdemeanor, or a class B misdemeanor when exceeding the posted speed limit by twenty miles per hour or more.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 11 editorial headings for 304.010 defining roadway categories, setting uniform maximum speed limits, governing MoDOT/municipal/county speed adjustments and signage, preserving pre-1996 local limits and emergency exemptions, and setting misdemeanor penalties.

headings.title: Prohibition on impeding traffic by slow speed and officer directions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits driving so slowly as to impede normal traffic unless necessary for safety or law compliance, and makes willful disobedience of a peace officer's direction a misdemeanor.

headings.title: Forty-mph interstate minimum speed and agricultural permit exception
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits operating below forty miles per hour on interstate highways except for weather/safety conditions or occasional short-distance agricultural implement operation under a section 304.200 special permit.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor penalty for interstate minimum speed violation
headings.reviewNote: Classifies any violation of subsection 2 of this section as a class C misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 304.011 prohibiting traffic-impeding slow driving, establishing the forty-mile-per-hour interstate minimum speed with weather and special-permit agricultural exceptions, and setting a class C misdemeanor penalty.

headings.title: Operation with highest degree of care
headings.reviewNote: Mandates operation of every vehicle in a careful and prudent manner.

headings.title: Prohibition on stunt driving on state roads and highways
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any motor vehicle operator on state roads and highways from performing stunt driving as defined in section 304.145.

headings.title: Class B misdemeanor or class A misdemeanor if accident involved
headings.reviewNote: Classifies a violation of this section as a class B misdemeanor, or a class A misdemeanor if an accident is involved.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 304.012 requiring the highest degree of care, prohibiting stunt driving under section 304.145, and setting class B and class A misdemeanor penalties.

headings.title: Prohibition on highway operation and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits all-terrain vehicles on public highways while providing narrow exceptions.

headings.title: Prohibition on off-road vehicles in streams or rivers and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Bars operating off-road vehicles in streams or rivers except on owned land, for agricultural purposes with ownership/permission, or fording at customary/highway crossings, enforced by peace officers, conservation agents, and DNR park rangers.

headings.title: License, thirty-mph limit, and bicycle safety flag requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires a valid operator's or chauffeur's license (with handicapped-person exception, no motorcycle exam), speed under 30 mph, and a seven-foot day-glow triangular bicycle safety flag on highways.

headings.title: Prohibitions on careless, intoxicated, or unhelmeted minor operation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits operating an ATV carelessly, under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances, or without a securely fastened safety helmet for individuals under age eighteen.

headings.title: Prohibition on ATV passengers and agricultural or multi-seat exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits ATV operators from carrying passengers except for agricultural purposes or on ATVs with seats designed for more than one person.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor and civil injunction or daily penalty
headings.reviewNote: Makes violation a class C misdemeanor and authorizes the attorney general or county prosecutor to seek injunctive relief and civil penalties up to one thousand dollars per day.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 editorial headings for 304.013 prohibiting ATV highway and stream/river operation with exceptions, requiring licenses/flags/30-mph limit, prohibiting careless/DWI/unhelmeted minor riding and passengers, and setting criminal and civil penalties.

headings.title: Right-side placement of parked vehicles not in motion
headings.reviewNote: Requires vehicles not in motion to be placed with their right side as near the right-hand side of the highway as practicable, except on municipal one-way or ordinance-regulated streets.

headings.title: Requirement to drive on right half
headings.reviewNote: Requires driving upon right half of roadway subject to statutory overtaking exceptions.

headings.title: Divided highway right-of-barrier travel and turn restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits driving except to the right of a divided highway's barrier/dividing section or making left or U-turns except at intersections, interchanges, or signed locations, exempting emergency, law enforcement, and commission/MoDOT vehicles.

headings.title: Temporary off-center traffic lane signs and officer directions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes highway authorities or the highway patrol to erect temporary off-center lane signs and direct conforming traffic, prohibiting disobedience of such signs.

headings.title: Rules for laned roadways and lane changes
headings.reviewNote: Governs driving within designated lanes and prohibits unsafe lane departures.

headings.title: Right-hand lane rule on highways with two or more lanes one way
headings.reviewNote: Requires vehicles on highways with two or more lanes in the same direction to drive in the right-hand lane except when overtaking, preparing a proper left turn, or directed by traffic markings, signs, or signals.

headings.title: Far-left lane ban for trucks over 48,000 pounds in urban areas
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits trucks registered over 48,000 pounds gross weight from the far left-hand lane on urbanized interstates, freeways, or expressways with three or more same-direction lanes, with traffic-control and construction exceptions.

headings.title: Definition of truck for far-left lane restriction
headings.reviewNote: Defines truck for subsection 7 to include property-transport vehicles, tractors, trailers, semitrailers, combinations, and commercial motor vehicles under section 301.010.

headings.title: Class C, B, and A misdemeanor penalties for lane violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violation as a class C misdemeanor, elevated to class B if causing immediate threat of an accident and class A if an accident results.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 editorial headings for 304.015 governing right-side parking, right-half driving, divided highway restrictions, temporary off-center lanes, multi-lane rules, heavy-truck left-lane restrictions, truck definition, and graduated misdemeanor penalties.

headings.title: Rules governing overtaking and passing vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Requires passing on the left and yielding right-of-way when being overtaken.

headings.title: Conditions permitting overtaking on the right
headings.reviewNote: Specifies situations where overtaking and passing on the right is permissible.

headings.title: Limitations on driving left of center
headings.reviewNote: Restricts driving on left side of roadway when overtaking obstructed view or hazards.

headings.title: Prohibition on driving left of center on grades, curves, or crossings
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits driving on the left side of the roadway when view is obstructed near a grade crest, curve, or within one hundred feet of a bridge, viaduct, tunnel, intersection, or railroad grade crossing.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor penalty for violations
headings.reviewNote: Establishes class C misdemeanor classification for passing and overtaking violations.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 editorial headings for 304.016 governing overtaking on left and right, clear-visibility center-line limits, grade/curve/bridge/intersection left-side bans, and class C misdemeanor penalty.

headings.title: Following distance rules and commercial spacing
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits following more closely than reasonable and sets spacing for trucks and caravans.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor penalty for violations
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that following too closely in violation of statute is a class C misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 304.017 governing safe following distance and caravan spacing (without affecting section 304.044) and class C misdemeanor penalty.

headings.title: Signaling requirements for stopping and turning
headings.reviewNote: Mandates signals when stopping or turning and specifies hand and mechanical methods.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor penalty for violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies failure to give required stop or turn signals as a class C misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 304.019 governing hand and mechanical stop and turn signals, vehicle dimension triggers for mechanical signals, and class C misdemeanor penalty.

headings.title: Driver duty to yield and pull right for approaching emergency vehicle
headings.reviewNote: Requires drivers to yield right-of-way, pull parallel to the right edge of the highway, and stop until an approaching emergency vehicle with siren or red/blue light passes, unless directed otherwise by an officer.

headings.title: Move over or slow down for stationary vehicles with warning lights
headings.reviewNote: Requires drivers approaching a stationary vehicle displaying red, red/blue, amber, or amber/white lights to change to a non-adjacent lane on four-or-more-lane roads if safe, or slow to a safe speed with due caution.

headings.title: Streetcar motorman duty to stop clear of intersection
headings.reviewNote: Requires every streetcar motorman to stop immediately clear of any intersection until an emergency vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by a police or traffic officer.

headings.title: Ten categories of vehicles defined as emergency vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Defines emergency vehicle across ten categories including law enforcement, fire, coroners/medical examiners, ambulances, section 307.175 vehicles, wreckers/utilities, extrication vehicles, emergency management, corrections, hazmat, MoDOT response, and National Guard civil support.

headings.title: Siren and light limits, emergency exemptions, and police exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Restricts siren/light use to emergencies/pursuits/fire responses, grants conditional parking, red-light, speed, and turning exemptions when using signals, and exempts police vehicles from signals during speeding enforcement, crime-in-progress response, or surveillance.

headings.title: Affidavit required to purchase emergency vehicle light
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits purchasing an emergency light described in this section without furnishing the seller an affidavit stating the light will be used exclusively for emergency vehicle purposes.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty for violations
headings.reviewNote: Deems any violation of this section to be a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 editorial headings for 304.022 governing yielding to approaching emergency vehicles, Move Over duties, streetcar stops, ten emergency vehicle categories, siren/light rules and exemptions, emergency light affidavits, and class A misdemeanor penalty.

headings.title: Rules for passing streetcars and safety zones
headings.reviewNote: Regulates passing streetcars discharging passengers and vehicle speed near safety zones.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor penalty for violations
headings.reviewNote: Provides that violation of streetcar passing rules constitutes a class C misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 304.023 governing stopping eight feet behind loading/unloading streetcars (with safety-zone exception) and class C misdemeanor penalty.

headings.title: Commission authority to sign crossovers, crosswalks, and parking bans
headings.reviewNote: Permits the highways and transportation commission to erect official signs establishing crossovers or crosswalks or prohibiting/restricting stopping, standing, or parking where dangerous or interfering with traffic, and bars violating such signs.

headings.title: Infraction classification for sign violations
headings.reviewNote: Deems a violation of this section to be an infraction.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 304.024 authorizing commission crosswalk, crossover, and parking restriction signs and classifying violations as infractions.

headings.title: Definition of highway for sections 304.014 to 304.026
headings.reviewNote: Defines highway for sections 304.014 to 304.026 as any public road or thoroughfare for vehicles, including state/county roads and municipal streets, avenues, boulevards, parkways, or alleys.

headings.title: Definition of vehicle for sections 304.014 to 304.026
headings.reviewNote: Defines vehicle for sections 304.014 to 304.026 as any device operated on highways except those used exclusively on rails or tracks.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 304.025 defining highway and vehicle for sections 304.014 to 304.026.

headings.title: Creation and research uses of Spinal Cord Injury Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Spinal Cord Injury Fund in the state treasury for University of Missouri curators' spinal cord injury research upon appropriation, exempt from biennial transfer to general revenue under section 33.080.

headings.title: Two-dollar criminal and traffic surcharge for Spinal Cord Injury Fund
headings.reviewNote: Assesses a two-dollar court cost surcharge in criminal, county ordinance, and state traffic cases (including infractions), excluding dismissals or public-paid costs, payable to the Spinal Cord Injury Fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 304.027 creating the Spinal Cord Injury Fund for University of Missouri research and imposing a two-dollar criminal and traffic court cost surcharge.

headings.title: Creation and community support uses of Brain Injury Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Brain Injury Fund in the state treasury for DHSS transition, integration, outreach, and community support services for traumatic brain injury individuals upon appropriation, exempt from section 33.080 biennial transfer.

headings.title: Two-dollar criminal and traffic court cost surcharge
headings.reviewNote: Assesses a two-dollar court cost surcharge in criminal, county ordinance, and state traffic cases (including infractions), excluding dismissals or cases where costs are paid by the state, county, or municipality.

headings.title: Clerk collection and deposit into Brain Injury Fund
headings.reviewNote: Directs the court clerk to collect and distribute the surcharge under sections 488.010 to 488.020 for deposit in the state treasury to the credit of the Brain Injury Fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 304.028 creating the Brain Injury Fund for DHSS community support services, imposing a two-dollar criminal and traffic surcharge, and directing clerk collection and deposit.

headings.title: Authorized highway operation, rights, and duties of low-speed vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Permits operating qualifying low-speed vehicles on state highways with all applicable motor vehicle driver rights and duties.

headings.title: Traffic law observance and thirty-five-mph highway speed limit
headings.reviewNote: Requires observing traffic laws and bars low-speed vehicles on streets or highways posted over thirty-five miles per hour, while allowing crossing such streets or highways.

headings.title: Exemption from inspection/registration rules and 49 CFR 571.500 compliance
headings.reviewNote: Exempts low-speed vehicles from sections 307.350 to 307.402 for titling and registration and requires compliance with 49 CFR 571.500.

headings.title: Mandatory chapter 303 financial responsibility for low-speed vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Requires every low-speed vehicle operator to maintain financial responsibility under chapter 303 when operating on state highways.

headings.title: Valid chapter 302 driver's license requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires each person operating a low-speed vehicle on a state highway to possess a valid driver's license issued under chapter 302.

headings.title: Federal 49 CFR 571.3 definition of low-speed vehicle
headings.reviewNote: Adopts the definition of low-speed vehicle set forth in 49 CFR Section 571.3, as amended.

headings.title: NHTSA manufacturing compliance under 49 CFR 571.500
headings.reviewNote: Requires all low-speed vehicles to be manufactured in compliance with NHTSA standards in 49 CFR 571.500, as amended.

headings.title: Stricter local ordinances and MoDOT public-safety prohibitions
headings.reviewNote: Preserves county and municipal authority to adopt more stringent ordinances and permits MoDOT to prohibit low-speed vehicles on highways under its jurisdiction for public safety.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 editorial headings for 304.029 governing low-speed vehicle highway operation, 35-mph limit, titling/registration exemption and 49 CFR 571.500 compliance, financial responsibility, driver's license, definition, manufacturing standards, and local/MoDOT restrictions.

headings.title: Definition of Traffic Signal Preemption System (TSPS)
headings.reviewNote: Defines Traffic Signal Preemption System (TSPS) as a traffic-control system designated for emergency vehicles to temporarily control signalized intersections.

headings.title: Signal owner authorization for emergency, bus, and maintenance TSPS
headings.reviewNote: Permits a traffic signal owner to authorize TSPS use by emergency vehicles or stations, buses extending green lights, and traffic signal maintenance vehicles.

headings.title: Emergency vehicle and station TSPS override priority
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an authorized emergency vehicle or station TSPS preempts and overrides any device operated by any other person.

headings.title: Release of signal upon arrival and defense for improper official use
headings.reviewNote: Requires TSPS devices to stop controlling the signal once the vehicle arrives at the intersection, and bars convicting a motorist where evidence shows improper government official TSPS signal manipulation.

headings.title: Prohibition on unauthorized TSPS traffic control
headings.reviewNote: Makes it unlawful for any person not approved under this section to use a TSPS to control traffic.

headings.title: Class B misdemeanor penalty for TSPS violations
headings.reviewNote: Deems any violation of this section to be a class B misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 editorial headings for 304.031 defining Traffic Signal Preemption Systems (TSPS), governing authorized signal-owner permissions, emergency override priority, arrival release and improper-use defense, unauthorized use ban, and class B misdemeanor penalty.

headings.title: Authorized highway operation of utility vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes utility vehicles on highways for maintenance, agriculture, and government use.

headings.title: Prohibition on utility vehicles in streams or rivers and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Bars operating utility vehicles in streams or rivers except on owned land, for agricultural purposes with ownership/permission, or fording at customary/highway crossings, enforced by peace officers, conservation agents, and DNR park rangers.

headings.title: Driver's license requirement and forty-five-mph speed cap
headings.reviewNote: Requires a valid operator's or chauffeur's license (with handicapped-person exception, no motorcycle exam) and operating speeds under forty-five miles per hour on highways.

headings.title: Prohibitions on careless or intoxicated utility vehicle operation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits operating a utility vehicle carelessly so as to endanger person or property, or while under the influence of alcohol or any controlled substance.

headings.title: Prohibition on passengers with agricultural and multi-seat exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits utility vehicle operators from carrying passengers except for agricultural purposes or on utility vehicles with seats designed for more than one person.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor and civil injunction or daily penalty
headings.reviewNote: Makes violation a class C misdemeanor and authorizes the attorney general or county prosecutor to seek injunctive relief and civil penalties up to one thousand dollars per day.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 editorial headings for 304.032 prohibiting utility vehicle highway and stream/river operation with exceptions, requiring licenses and under-45-mph speed, banning careless/DWI operation and passengers, and setting criminal and civil penalties.

headings.title: General prohibition on highway vehicle operation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits recreational off-highway vehicles on highways with agricultural exceptions.

headings.title: Prohibition on recreational off-highway vehicles in streams or rivers
headings.reviewNote: Bars operating recreational off-highway vehicles in streams or rivers except on owned land, for agricultural purposes with ownership/permission, or fording at customary/highway crossings, enforced by peace officers, conservation agents, and DNR park rangers.

headings.title: License, lighting, seat belt, and roll bar or roll cage requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires a valid license (with handicapped-person exception, no motorcycle exam), lighted headlamp and taillamp, seat belt use, and roll bar or roll cage construction on highways; source footnote notes original rolls of H.B. 1807 (2012) read 'upon on'.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 304.033 prohibiting recreational off-highway vehicles on highways and in streams/rivers with exceptions, and requiring licenses, headlamps/taillamps, seat belts, and roll bars/cages.

headings.title: Municipal authorization for golf carts and motorized wheelchairs
headings.reviewNote: Permits municipalities by resolution or ordinance to allow golf carts or motorized wheelchairs on local streets, barring state/federal highway operation except crossing intersections posted at forty-five miles per hour or less.

headings.title: Brake and local safety rules and chapter 301 registration exemption
headings.reviewNote: Requires golf carts on city streets to have adequate brakes and meet local safety requirements, and exempts them from chapter 301 registration.

headings.title: Definition of golf cart
headings.reviewNote: Defines golf cart as a motor vehicle designed and manufactured for golf course sporting or recreational operation incapable of exceeding twenty miles per hour.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 304.034 authorizing municipal ordinances for golf carts and motorized wheelchairs, setting brake/safety and chapter 301 exemption rules, and defining golf cart.

headings.title: Mandatory fifteen-to-fifty-foot stop at railroad grade crossings
headings.reviewNote: Requires drivers to stop fifteen to fifty feet from the nearest rail and not proceed until safe when warned by signals, lowered gates/flagmen, visibly hazardous trains, or other traffic signs/rules.

headings.title: Prohibition on driving around or under closed railroad crossing gates
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits driving through, around, or under a railroad crossing gate or barrier when a train is approaching while the gate is closed or being opened or closed.

headings.title: Sufficient space required to clear railroad crossing completely
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits driving through a railroad crossing without sufficient space to drive completely through the crossing.

headings.title: Sufficient undercarriage clearance required at railroad crossings
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits driving through a railroad crossing unless the vehicle has sufficient undercarriage clearance to prevent contacting the crossing.

headings.title: Commercial motor vehicle speed and due caution at railroad crossings
headings.reviewNote: Requires commercial motor vehicles (except those required to stop under section 304.030) to approach railroad crossings at a speed permitting stopping before the nearest rail and proceed only after due caution.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor penalty for railroad crossing violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies any violation of this section as a class C misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 editorial headings for 304.035 governing mandatory stops at railroad grade crossings, crossing gate bans, clearance and space rules, commercial vehicle crossing speeds, and class C misdemeanor penalty.

headings.title: Definitions of bus and truck
headings.reviewNote: Defines bus (carrying more than seven persons) and truck (mechanical-power property-transport vehicle or combination) for this section.

headings.title: Three-hundred-foot following distance outside urban districts
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits trucks and buses outside business or residential districts from following within three hundred feet of another such vehicle, while permitting overtaking and passing.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor penalty for violations
headings.reviewNote: Designates violation of commercial truck spacing requirements as a class C misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 304.044 defining bus and truck, prohibiting following within three hundred feet outside business/residential districts (except overtaking), and setting a class C misdemeanor penalty.

headings.title: Driver duty to stop for school bus
headings.reviewNote: Requires drivers meeting or overtaking a stopped school bus with stop signal to stop until motion resumes or signaled, and includes certified Head Start buses operated by CDL-endorsed drivers.

headings.title: Required school bus signs, rear lettering, and signaling devices
headings.reviewNote: Requires front/rear eight-inch 'school bus' signs, rear 'State Law: Stop while bus is loading and unloading' lettering, and state-board-approved mechanical and electrical stop-signaling devices.

headings.title: Crossing control arm requirement (Jessica's Law)
headings.reviewNote: Requires specified public school buses over 10,000 pounds GVWR to have a right-front crossing control arm extending at least five feet six inches by August 1, 1998, cited as Jessica's Law.

headings.title: Signal activation during loading and four-lane pull-off policy
headings.reviewNote: Requires activating stop signals during loading/unloading, while authorizing school districts to adopt policies allowing four-or-more-lane divided-highway pull-offs using amber/emergency flashers where students cross no lanes.

headings.title: Lane-crossing limit and visibility requirements for bus stops
headings.reviewNote: Bars loading/unloading requiring crossing more than two lanes on four-or-more-lane highways and requires 500-foot visibility (no shoulder, >60 mph) or 300-foot visibility (other highways) only while actually loading/unloading.

headings.title: Exceptions on separate roadways, four-lane opposite traffic, and zones
headings.reviewNote: Exempts drivers from stopping for a school bus on a separate roadway, proceeding in the opposite direction on a four-or-more-lane highway, or in a no-pedestrian-crossing loading zone on a limited-access highway.

headings.title: Bus driver duty to remain stopped for three or more following vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Requires a school bus driver after loading or unloading to remain stopped to let three or more following vehicles pass when safe to do so.

headings.title: Rebuttable presumption of registered owner identity and rental rebuttal
headings.reviewNote: Creates a rebuttable presumption that the registered owner committed a witnessed violation (limiting conviction/costs to one co-owner) and allows rental/leasing companies to rebut by furnishing the agreement within fifteen days of registered-mail notice.

headings.title: Requirement for two license plates on every school bus
headings.reviewNote: Requires every school bus to have two license plates notwithstanding section 301.130.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 editorial headings for 304.050 governing stopping for school and Head Start buses, bus signs/signals, crossing control arms (Jessica's Law), loading/unloading rules, divided-highway exceptions, pulling over for three vehicles, owner presumption, and two license plates.

headings.title: State board authority over bus standards
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes state board of education to adopt uniform design and safety regulations for buses.

headings.title: Urban school district contracts for additional high school transit
headings.reviewNote: Permits school boards in urban districts containing most of a city over 300,000 to contract with municipalities, bi-state agencies, or governmental entities for supplemental grade 9–12 transportation.

headings.title: Employee removal and contractor cancellation for noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Makes school officer/employee violation or omission of compliance terms misconduct subject to removal, and requires cancelling noncompliant bus contractor contracts after notice and hearing.

headings.title: Use of word 'special' on school buses in charter county adjoining city
headings.reviewNote: Permits school buses in a first-class charter county adjoining a city not within a county to bear the word 'special'.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 editorial headings for 304.060 governing state board of education bus and alternative-vehicle regulations, urban district high-school transit contracts, employee/contractor noncompliance, and St. Louis County 'special' bus signs.

headings.title: Misdemeanor and felony penalties and injury definitions
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violating section 304.050(1), (3), or (7) as a class A misdemeanor, elevating subsection 1 violations to a class E felony for child physical injury and class D felony for serious physical injury or death, and defines those terms.

headings.title: Mandatory non-suspendable graduated fines for passing school buses
headings.reviewNote: Imposes non-suspendable fines for section 304.050(1) violations: $500–$1,000 (first offense), $1,000–$2,000 (second within five years), and $1,500–$3,000 (third or subsequent within five years).

headings.title: Mandatory open-court appearance for school bus passing violations
headings.reviewNote: Bars disposing of section 304.050(1) violations through the fine collection center or fine payment without open-court appearance in person or by attorney.

headings.title: Discretionary first-offense and mandatory repeat license suspensions
headings.reviewNote: Permits court-ordered DOR license suspension for a first section 304.050(1) violation and mandates 90-day (second within five years) and 180-day (third or subsequent within five years) suspensions in addition to chapter 302 penalties.

headings.title: Cumulative application of fines and suspensions to injury or death cases
headings.reviewNote: Applies subsection 2 fines and subsection 4 suspensions to all section 304.050(1) violations, including those causing child injury or death, in addition to subsection 1 penalties.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 editorial headings for 304.070 establishing misdemeanor and felony penalties for section 304.050 violations, non-suspendable graduated fines, mandatory court appearances, license suspensions, and cumulative application.

headings.title: Prohibition on school bus signs when not transporting school children
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits non-school-bus vehicles from bearing school bus signs and requires contract bus operators to cover signs when using a bus for non-school-child purposes.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor penalty for school bus sign violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies any violation of this section as a class C misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 304.075 requiring removal or covering of school bus signs when not transporting school children and setting a class C misdemeanor penalty.

headings.title: Authorized use of designated disabled parking spaces
headings.reviewNote: Restricts disabled parking spaces to vehicles displaying section 301.142 or reciprocal plates/placards when the disabled holder is an occupant or is being delivered or collected.

headings.title: Duty to produce disabled registration certificate and photo ID
headings.reviewNote: Requires the driver or occupant of a vehicle parked in a disabled space to produce the section 301.142 disabled registration certificate and photo identification of the disabled person upon peace officer request.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty and valid-certificate court defense
headings.reviewNote: Makes inability to produce proper authorization a class A misdemeanor, but bars conviction if the operator produces to the court a certificate valid at the time of citation for a person using the vehicle.

headings.title: Prohibition on driving with windshield hanging placard on mirror
headings.reviewNote: Limits windshield hanging placard display to parked disabled spaces and makes operating a motor vehicle with a placard hanging from the inside rearview mirror unlawful.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 editorial headings for 304.079 restricting disabled parking space use, requiring certificate and photo ID production on officer request, setting a class A misdemeanor with court-production defense, and barring driving with hanging placards.

headings.title: Municipal authority to regulate local traffic
headings.reviewNote: Permits municipalities by ordinance to set reasonable speed limits, requiring specified boundary signs to convict nonresidents present forty-eight hours or less.

headings.title: Regulation of speed, parking, and stops
headings.reviewNote: Empowers municipalities to limit vehicle speed, establish one-way streets, and regulate parking.

headings.title: Invalidity of municipal ordinances conflicting with chapter 304
headings.reviewNote: Declares invalid any municipal ordinance containing provisions contrary to or in conflict with chapter 304, except as provided in this section.

headings.title: Exemption of motor vehicle owner-lessors providing lessee information
headings.reviewNote: Bars municipal ordinances from holding an owner-lessor liable for a lessee's violation if the lessor supplies lessee details within three working days of written request, except for inoperable vehicle defects not caused by the lessee.

headings.title: Prohibition on denying commercial vehicles all municipal routes
headings.reviewNote: Bars ordinances from denying commercial motor vehicles use of all routes within a municipality and defines route.

headings.title: Preemption of local ordinances barring yellow-light intersection entry
headings.reviewNote: Bars ordinances from prohibiting being in an intersection during a red signal after entering during a yellow interval, superseding contrary local laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 editorial headings for 304.120 governing municipal speed ordinances and boundary signs, eight enumerated local traffic powers, conflict invalidity, owner-lessor liability exemption, commercial route access, and yellow-light intersection preemption.

headings.title: County commission traffic regulation authority
headings.reviewNote: Empowers county commissions in first-class counties to adopt traffic and congested-area speed regulations in unincorporated areas consistent with state motor vehicle laws.

headings.title: Public hearings, fifteen-day notice, and highway commission approval
headings.reviewNote: Requires three public hearings with fifteen-day newspaper and posted notice before adopting regulations (except subsection 3), and requires highways and transportation commission approval for stop signs, signals, and speed limits on state or federal highways.

headings.title: Procedural exemption for regulations solely increasing speed limits
headings.reviewNote: Exempts regulations relating solely to increasing speed limits from subsection 2 hearing/notice procedures, making them effective immediately upon county commission approval.

headings.title: Codification, distribution, and speed-limit boundary sign posting
headings.reviewNote: Requires adopted regulations to be codified, printed, and distributed for public use and requires posting speed-limit signs where limits begin and end.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 editorial headings for 304.130 authorizing first-class county traffic regulations, three public hearings and commission approval, exemption for speed-limit increases, and codification/signage requirements.

headings.title: Definitions of stunt driving, street takeover, and offender tiers
headings.reviewNote: Defines fourteen terms including aggravated, chronic, habitual, persistent, and prior offenders, burnout, donut, drag race, drifting, highway, race, street takeover, stunt driving, and wheelie.

headings.title: Prohibition on street takeovers and related stunt driving
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits performing stunt driving in connection with a street takeover or performing or participating in a street takeover, except as permitted by law.

headings.title: Graduated misdemeanor and felony penalties for repeat offenses
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violation as a class B misdemeanor (first offense), class A misdemeanor (second offense), and class E felony (third or subsequent offense).

headings.title: Bar on suspended imposition of sentence or fine-only for repeat offenders
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits granting suspended imposition of sentence or fine in lieu of imprisonment to proven prior, persistent, aggravated, chronic, or habitual offenders.

headings.title: Ten-day minimum imprisonment or thirty-day community service for priors
headings.reviewNote: Bars probation or parole for proven prior offenders until serving ten days' imprisonment unless performing at least thirty days of court-supervised community service.

headings.title: Thirty-day minimum imprisonment for aggravated offenders
headings.reviewNote: Bars probation or parole eligibility for proven aggravated offenders until serving a minimum of thirty days' imprisonment.

headings.title: One-year minimum imprisonment for chronic or habitual offenders
headings.reviewNote: Bars probation or parole eligibility for proven chronic or habitual offenders until serving a minimum of one year's imprisonment.

headings.title: Pleading and proving prior offenses under section 558.021
headings.reviewNote: Requires prior pleas and findings of guilty to be pleaded and proven in the same manner as required by section 558.021.

headings.title: Exemption for sanctioned events on controlled highways or private property
headings.reviewNote: Exempts events sanctioned by a political subdivision or private entity responsible for maintenance and control of the highway portion or private property.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 editorial headings for 304.145 defining stunt driving, street takeovers, and repeat-offender tiers, prohibiting street takeovers and related stunt driving, setting penalties and imprisonment/parole floors, and exempting sanctioned events.

headings.title: Driver duty to move vehicle obstructing state highway traffic
headings.reviewNote: Requires the driver of a vehicle obstructing regular traffic on any state highway, except in accidents involving injury or death, to make every reasonable effort to move it out of traffic.

headings.title: Pre-1999 written warning and post-1999 infraction fine
headings.reviewNote: Required written warnings prior to January 1, 1999, and beginning January 1, 1999, classifies noncompliance as an infraction punishable by a fine of ten to fifty dollars.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 304.151 requiring drivers to move vehicles obstructing state highway traffic (except injury/death accidents) and establishing pre-1999 warnings and post-1999 infraction fines.

headings.title: Prohibition on vehicle-type roadside checkpoints including motorcycles
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits law enforcement agencies from establishing roadside checkpoints or roadblock patterns based on a particular vehicle type, including motorcycle-only checkpoints.

headings.title: Exception for commercial motor vehicle roadside checkpoints
headings.reviewNote: Permits law enforcement agencies to establish roadside checkpoint patterns stopping and checking only commercial motor vehicles as defined in section 301.010.

headings.title: Preservation of other lawful constitutional checkpoints
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section does not restrict any other lawful checkpoint or roadblock operated in accordance with the U.S. and Missouri Constitutions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 editorial headings for 304.152 prohibiting vehicle-type roadside checkpoints (including motorcycle-only), allowing commercial motor vehicle checkpoints, and preserving other constitutional checkpoints.

headings.title: Definitions for law enforcement and agency towing utilization
headings.reviewNote: Defines nine terms: firefighter, law enforcement officer, motor club, patrol officer, tow list, tow management company, tow truck, towing, and towing company.

headings.title: Use of tow lists or management companies and owner tow requests
headings.reviewNote: Permits officers, St. Louis firefighters, and MoDOT employees to use tow lists or management companies, allows highway patrol removal from tow lists at any time, and requires honoring owner/operator tow requests absent unreasonable delay or immediate traffic hazard.

headings.title: Restrictions on using out-of-state towing companies
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits patrol officers and St. Louis firefighters from using out-of-state towing companies except during a declared state/federal emergency or upon driver, owner, or motor club request.

headings.title: Prohibition on towing vehicles outside Missouri without consent
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a towing company from towing a vehicle outside Missouri without consent of the driver, owner, or their motor club.

headings.title: Prohibition on unsolicited towing from accident scenes
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits uncalled towing companies or tow trucks from towing vehicles from accident scenes unless rendering emergency public-safety aid or operating during a section 44.100 declared state of emergency.

headings.title: Graduated misdemeanor, felony, and impounding penalties
headings.reviewNote: Penalizes violating subsection 5 as a class D misdemeanor with tow truck impounding (first), class A misdemeanor (second), and class D felony (third or subsequent), without precluding chapter 569 tampering charges.

headings.title: Applicability to vehicles towed under sections 304.155 and 304.157
headings.reviewNote: Applies this section to motor vehicles towed under section 304.155 or 304.157.

headings.title: Inapplicability to third and fourth classification counties
headings.reviewNote: Exempts counties of the third or fourth classification from this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 editorial headings for 304.153 governing law enforcement, St. Louis firefighter, and MoDOT use of tow lists/management companies, owner tow requests, out-of-state towing limits, unsolicited accident-scene towing penalties, and county applicability.

headings.title: Ten operational, business-hour, insurance, and rate-sheet requirements
headings.reviewNote: Sets ten requirements for towing companies under sections 304.153, 304.155, or 304.157 including visible address, secure storage, 10-hour M–F availability, 24-hour location notice, 24/7 dispatch, $500,000 liability coverage, workers' comp, truck registrations, and posted rate sheet.

headings.title: Requirement that initial tow remain within Missouri
headings.reviewNote: Requires initial tows under section 304.153, 304.155, or 304.157 to remain in Missouri unless authorized by the vehicle owner, authorized agent, or motor club.

headings.title: Additional county ordinances and exemption for 2nd–4th class counties
headings.reviewNote: Permits counties to adopt additional towing standards and exempts towing companies located in second, third, or fourth classification counties from this section.

headings.title: Free access and inspection for insurance adjusters during business hours
headings.reviewNote: Requires storage lots and towing companies to allow insurance adjusters free access and inspection during normal business hours unless law enforcement notifies them the vehicle is preserved as evidence.

headings.title: Twenty-four-hour advance owner notice before storage lot transfer
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits transferring a towed vehicle from a storage lot/facility without twenty-four-hour advance notice to the owner stating the new address and all transfer costs.

headings.title: Partial inapplicability to third and fourth classification counties
headings.reviewNote: Exempts third and fourth classification counties from subdivisions (3), (4), (6), and (10) of subsection 1, visible-address display in (1), and subsections 2, 4, and 5.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 editorial headings for 304.154 setting ten towing company operational/insurance/rate-sheet requirements, in-state initial tow rule, county ordinances and exemptions, free adjuster access, and 24-hour transfer notices (effective 10-14-16 via veto override).

headings.title: Law enforcement authority to tow abandoned vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes law enforcement officers to remove vehicles left unattended on highways.

headings.title: Immediate hazard removal by MoDOT or law enforcement and CMV rule
headings.reviewNote: Permits MoDOT or law enforcement to immediately remove wrecked/spilled traffic hazards from state highways, limiting MoDOT removal of non-hazmat commercial motor vehicles to a place of safety pending owner tow-company choice.

headings.title: Crime inquiry and inspection reports and two-hour agency notices
headings.reviewNote: Requires law enforcement agencies to complete a crime inquiry and inspection report for removals from the immediate vicinity, and requires non-law-enforcement agencies to report to patrol or local police within two hours.

headings.title: Limited liability for officers, agencies, and custodians during removal
headings.reviewNote: Shields officers, government officials, and custodians from damage liability for authorized removals except for negligence or willful or wanton acts or omissions.

headings.title: Owner liability for reasonable towing and storage charges
headings.reviewNote: Makes the owner of abandoned property removed under this section or section 304.157 responsible for reasonable towing and storage charges as provided in section 304.158.

headings.title: NCIC stolen checks, ten-day DOR inquiries, and ten report elements
headings.reviewNote: Requires prompt NCIC/statewide stolen-vehicle checks, ten-working-day online DOR inquiries or law enforcement report submission to DOR, and specifies ten required crime inquiry and inspection report elements.

headings.title: Three-year retention of crime inquiry and inspection report copies
headings.reviewNote: Requires retaining report copies with the authorizing agency, storage facility, and towing facility in accessible business records for three years.

headings.title: Reclamation by owner or lienholder upon proof and payment
headings.reviewNote: Permits the owner or holder of a valid security interest of record to reclaim abandoned property upon proof of ownership or security interest and payment of reasonable towing and storage charges.

headings.title: Towing and storage lien, personal property release, and medication rule
headings.reviewNote: Grants a lien for reasonable towing and storage charges enforced under section 304.156, requires releasing prescribed medication upon request, and imposes strict liability for safe return of personal property.

headings.title: Three-year towing company recordkeeping for unclaimed property
headings.reviewNote: Requires towing companies to keep three-year records of tow authorization, DOR correspondence, online record inquiries, and final disposition for unclaimed abandoned property.

headings.title: Two-hour law enforcement notice for nonconsensual repossessions
headings.reviewNote: Requires lienholders repossessing vehicles or vessels without owner knowledge/cooperation to notify local law enforcement within two hours for NCIC/statewide entry.

headings.title: Disposal of unclaimed vehicles after notice
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes disposal of unclaimed abandoned vehicles in accordance with statutory procedures.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 12 editorial headings for 304.155 governing law enforcement/agency abandoned vehicle towing on public property and waters, hazard removal, reports, limited liability, owner charges, NCIC/DOR checks, reclamation, liens, 3-year records, repossession notices, and 30-day scrap disposal.

headings.title: Notice requirement to owner and lienholders
headings.reviewNote: Requires DOR record search within five working days and notice to the tower within fifteen working days, and requires the towing company to send certified-mail notice with eight specified disclosures within ten business days.

headings.title: Limits on nonconsensual reasonable storage charges
headings.reviewNote: Limits nonconsensual storage charges to reasonable negotiated consent rates and allows assessment only during compliance with sections 304.155 to 304.158.

headings.title: Physical search and four good-faith checks when owner unknown
headings.reviewNote: Requires towing companies to physically search abandoned property and certify four good-faith checks for prior state registration/title when DOR records disclose no owner or lienholder.

headings.title: Written DOR notice and title application if no ownership found
headings.reviewNote: Directs notifying the director of revenue in writing and obtaining title under subsection 7 if no ownership information is discovered.

headings.title: Ten-day wrongful-taking petition, bond release, and final fee order
headings.reviewNote: Permits owners or lienholders within ten days of notice to petition associate circuit court to contest wrongful taking, bars DOR title issuance pending decision, allows release upon posting bond, and directs final fee orders.

headings.title: Enforcement of towing and storage lien under subsection 7
headings.reviewNote: Directs that a towing and storage lien be enforced as provided in subsection 7.

headings.title: Thirty-day title application and five required supporting documents
headings.reviewNote: Permits lienholders in possession to apply to DOR for a certificate thirty days after mailing notice if unredeemed and no hearing requested, with required affidavits, reports, and certified-mail records.

headings.title: Good-faith search required when certified notice returned undeliverable
headings.reviewNote: Requires lienholders in possession to comply with subsection 3 physical search checks when notice is returned marked 'not forwardable' or 'addressee unknown'.

headings.title: Municipal and county abandoned-property ordinances and Kansas City rules
headings.reviewNote: Permits consistent local removal/sale ordinances and specifies four mandatory search, mail-notice, 10-day low-value damaged-vehicle, and 30-day hold provisions for home rule cities over 400,000 in multiple counties.

headings.title: Local government bill of sale transfer and thirty-day title duty
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes municipalities and counties to transfer ownership by sealed clerk bill of sale, requires purchasers to apply for a certificate within thirty days, and makes violations an infraction.

headings.title: Transitional title applications until 2000 for pre-August 28, 1996 tows
headings.reviewNote: Permitted persons who towed abandoned property prior to August 28, 1996, to apply to DOR until January 1, 2000, with notarized affidavit, inspection, and certified-mail documentation.

headings.title: Issuance of original, prior-salvage, salvage, or junking certificates
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director of revenue, if satisfied with the application, to issue an original title, prior-salvage title, salvage/abandoned property or junking certificate, or upgraded original title after examination.

headings.title: Total-loss insurer removal or title transfer within thirty days
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurers or lienholders after paying a total-loss claim to remove property or transfer title within thirty days, governs reasonable fee payment, and requires insurers to disclose coverage responsibility on request.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 13 editorial headings for 304.156 governing DOR owner/lienholder notices, reasonable storage limits, physical vehicle searches, wrongful-taking court petitions and bonds, 30-day title applications, local ordinances and bills of sale, title issuance, and total-loss insurer duties.

headings.title: Law enforcement towing from private property after 48 hours or hazard
headings.reviewNote: Permits law enforcement officers (source footnote notes state water patrol changed to water patrol division in 2010) at a possessor's request to authorize towing abandoned property left over 48 hours or posing a hazard/interference.

headings.title: Local government derelict-vehicle ordinance towing and two-hour report
headings.reviewNote: Permits local agencies to tow derelict/junk vehicles or vessels under local ordinance and requires reporting to local law enforcement within two hours with a section 304.155 report.

headings.title: Limited liability for officers, local agencies, and custodians
headings.reviewNote: Shields officers, local agencies, and custodians from damage liability for authorized removals except for negligence or willful or wanton acts or omissions.

headings.title: Private landowner towing without officer under signage or wait rules
headings.reviewNote: Permits present landowners, lessees, or full-time property/security managers to authorize towing without law enforcement if 17x22-inch warning signs are posted, or after police notice plus 10 hours (small residential) or 96 hours (other private property).

headings.title: Abandoned property report legal declaration and eleven required items
headings.reviewNote: Requires landowners/lessees requesting non-officer tows to complete a DOR abandoned property report subject to section 575.060 false-declaration penalties containing eleven specified items.

headings.title: Towing company delivery of report within two or twenty-four hours
headings.reviewNote: Requires towing companies to deliver the report (including by fax if registered, except in 3rd/4th class counties) to local police within two hours for signed-lot tows or twenty-four hours otherwise.

headings.title: Law enforcement filing, NCIC stolen check, and signed report copy
headings.reviewNote: Requires police to record filing date, run NCIC/statewide stolen checks, enter towed data, and return a signed copy; permits DOR to sell informational brochures.

headings.title: DOR record search and ten-day report transmittal for unclaimed vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Requires police to search DOR records and share owner/lienholder info, directs online towers to comply with 'section 301.155' (archived footnote notes section 301.155 does not exist), and requires sending signed reports to DOR after ten working days.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor for knowingly unauthorized landowner tow
headings.reviewNote: Makes an owner or lessee of real property who knowingly authorizes removal in violation of this section guilty of a class C misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 editorial headings for 304.157 governing law enforcement, local derelict-ordinance, and private landowner towing from private property, abandoned property reports, law enforcement filing and stolen checks, DOR reporting, and class C misdemeanor penalty.

headings.title: Five-working-day written removal notice to owner and lienholder
headings.reviewNote: Requires the authorizing public agency or towing company (for private tows) to send written notice within five working days with grounds, location, and mileage, plus a copy to the storage operator.

headings.title: Landowner duty to state grounds and towing company liability
headings.reviewNote: Requires landowners to state removal grounds on request, shields towers acting under present written authorization from validity claims, and holds towers liable for transit/storage damage or towing the wrong property.

headings.title: Vehicle owner recovery for property damage during removal
headings.reviewNote: Permits the owner of abandoned property removed from private property to recover for any damage resulting from any act of a person causing or performing removal.

headings.title: Landowner double-charge liability for statutory noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Holds a private property owner liable to the vehicle owner for double towing or storage charges upon failing to comply with this section or section 304.157.

headings.title: Three-inch company name, city, and state lettering on tow trucks
headings.reviewNote: Requires for-hire towing companies to display their name, city, and state in letters at least three inches high on the sides of towing vehicles.

headings.title: Half-price drop fee if owner returns before removal from property
headings.reviewNote: Caps the towing fee at one-half the regular charge if the owner or agent returns before removal from private property, permitting the full charge only once in transit.

headings.title: Mandatory cash acceptance and change at storage facilities
headings.reviewNote: Requires storage facility operators to accept cash for towing and storage charges and keep sufficient moneys on premises to make change.

headings.title: Written landowner authorization required and fire-lane exception
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits non-police private tows without prior written landowner authorization retained for one year, barring delegated blanket towing except within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant or in a designated fire lane.

headings.title: Quadruple-charge liability for towing without written authorization
headings.reviewNote: Holds any towing company or affiliate towing from private property without required present written authorization liable to the vehicle owner for four times towing and storage charges plus criminal penalties.

headings.title: Local ordinances setting maximum reasonable towing and storage charges
headings.reviewNote: Permits counties, cities, towns, and villages to enact consistent ordinances specifying maximum reasonable towing, storage, and other charges.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor, section 407.020 violation, and license revocation
headings.reviewNote: Makes knowing violation of sections 304.155 to 304.158 a class A misdemeanor, deems section violations section 407.020 merchandising practices violations, and authorizes court revocation/suspension of towing licenses in attorney general actions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 11 editorial headings for 304.158 governing 5-day removal notices, landowner/tower duties and damage liability, wrecker lettering, half-price drop fees, cash acceptance, written tow authorizations, quadruple damages, local fee ordinances, and class A misdemeanor/407.020 penalties.

headings.title: Duty to clear glass, tacks, or injurious substances from highway
headings.reviewNote: Requires any person who purposely, accidentally, or by accident drops tacks, nails, wire, scrap metal, glass, crockery, sharp stones, or other injurious substances on a highway to immediately make all reasonable efforts to clear them.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor penalty for failure to clear substances
headings.reviewNote: Deems any violation of this section to be a class C misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 editorial headings for 304.160 requiring immediate removal of glass, tacks, or injurious substances dropped on highways and classifying violations as a class C misdemeanor.

headings.title: Maximum vehicle width and safety device exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Limits vehicle width to 102 inches excluding safety devices and mirrors.

headings.title: Maximum vehicle height limitations and clearances
headings.reviewNote: Caps height including load at fourteen feet on interstates and commission-designated routes and thirteen and one-half feet on other highways, except fourteen feet for automobile transporters.

headings.title: Single vehicle length limits and bumper extensions
headings.reviewNote: Restricts single motor vehicle length to forty-five feet excluding bumpers.

headings.title: Bus, recreational vehicle, and articulated bus length limits
headings.reviewNote: Caps buses, RVs, and trackless trolleys at 45 feet (plus 1-foot front/rear safety bumpers) and permits articulated buses up to 60 feet excluding safety bumpers and 5-foot bicycle racks.

headings.title: Truck-tractor and semitrailer combination length limits
headings.reviewNote: Caps truck-tractor/semitrailer (or dromedary) combinations at 60 feet generally, and on interstates limits semitrailer length to 53 feet with no overall cap under P.L. 97-424.

headings.title: Truck-tractor, semitrailer, and trailer double combination limits
headings.reviewNote: Limits interstate twin trailers to 28 feet each (or 28.5 feet if operating Dec. 1, 1982) and caps combinations at 65 feet on nondesignated primary highways.

headings.title: Automobile and boat transporter lengths, overhang, and backhaul
headings.reviewNote: Permits 75-foot auto/boat transporters (3-ft front/4-ft rear overhang) and 80-foot stinger-steered auto transporters (4-ft front/6-ft rear overhang) on interstates/designated routes plus 10 miles, and allows general freight backhauls.

headings.title: Ninety-seven-foot driveaway saddlemount combination limits
headings.reviewNote: Permits driveaway saddlemount combinations up to 97 feet (max three saddlemounted and one fullmount, complying with 49 CFR 393.71) on interstates/designated routes plus 10 miles.

headings.title: Semitrailer-semitrailer combinations and B-train assembly exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Limits twin semitrailers to 28 feet (or 28.5 feet if operating Dec. 1, 1982) and excludes the B-train assembly from semitrailer length when connecting two semitrailers.

headings.title: Eighty-two-foot towaway trailer transporter combination limit
headings.reviewNote: Caps towaway trailer transporter combinations on interstates and designated primary highways at eighty-two feet overall length.

headings.title: Commission route designations and ten-mile access distance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to designate non-interstate routes for subsection 5–10 combinations and allows travel up to ten miles from interstates and designated routes.

headings.title: Length limits for other vehicle combinations on highways
headings.reviewNote: Caps other vehicle combinations at sixty-five feet on primary or interstate highways plus ten miles, and fifty-five feet on any other highway.

headings.title: Agricultural implement, cotton trailer, dealer, and lighting exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Exempts occasional agricultural implements/parades, hay/husbandry/farm products, 93-foot cotton/drought-hay trailers, and non-interstate implement dealer deliveries, and permits nighttime agricultural operation with section 307.115 lighting.

headings.title: Definition of implements of husbandry for chapter 304
headings.reviewNote: Defines implements of husbandry as self-propelled machinery under 30 mph designed/adapted for primary offroad use exclusively applying commercial plant food or agricultural chemicals.

headings.title: Sludge disposal units width limit and special permits
headings.reviewNote: Permits sludge disposal units up to 138 inches wide (observing axle weight limits) on non-interstate state highways under commission special permits restricting routes, days, and hours.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 15 editorial headings for 304.170 governing vehicle width, height, and length limits across single vehicles, buses, combinations, auto/boat transporters, saddlemounts, B-trains, towaways, route designations, agricultural exemptions, implements of husbandry, and sludge units.

headings.title: Single axle, steering axle, and tandem axle weight limits
headings.reviewNote: Caps single axles at 20,000 pounds, general-freight regular-route steering axles at 12,000 pounds/manufacturer rating, and tandem axles (40–96 inches apart) at 34,000 pounds.

headings.title: Definition of axle load
headings.reviewNote: Defines axle load as the total load transmitted to the road by all wheels whose centers lie between two parallel transverse vertical planes forty inches apart.

headings.title: Consecutive axle group gross weight table and consecutive tandem rule
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the embedded maximum gross weight table (34,000 to 80,000 pounds across 2–6 axles and 4–57 feet) and permits two consecutive 34,000-pound tandem sets spaced thirty-six feet or more apart.

headings.title: Commission weight and speed limits on endangered state highway bridges
headings.reviewNote: Permits the commission to post reduced maximum weight and speed limits on endangered state highway bridges, and allows cities or counties to authorize commission limits on local roadways.

headings.title: Federal P.L. 97-424 ceiling on axle and gross loads
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not permit axle, tandem, or gross loads exceeding federal limits under P.L. 97-424 (23 U.S.C. Section 101 et al.).

headings.title: Two-thousand-pound weight tolerance on non-interstate highways
headings.reviewNote: Permits exceeding single, tandem, and gross weight limits by up to 2,000 pounds on non-interstate highways, capped at 80,000 pounds gross except under subsections 9, 10, 12, 13, and 14.

headings.title: Special permits for cranes, concrete pump trucks, and well-drillers
headings.reviewNote: Requires the commission to issue single-use or annual special permits for cranes, concrete pump trucks, and well-drillers' equipment, permitting operation on state-maintained roads at any time on any day.

headings.title: Five-hundred-fifty-pound idle reduction technology weight allowance
headings.reviewNote: Permits increasing gross and axle weight limits by up to 550 pounds for functional idle reduction technology under 23 U.S.C. Section 127 upon proof to law enforcement.

headings.title: Eighty-five-thousand-five-hundred-pound non-interstate milk and livestock
headings.reviewNote: Permits vehicles hauling farm-to-processor milk or livestock up to 85,500 pounds gross weight on non-interstate highways, excluding the interstate system.

headings.title: Ten-percent non-interstate harvest grain and coproduct allowance
headings.reviewNote: Permits vehicles hauling grain or grain coproducts during harvest up to ten percent over subsection 3 limits on non-interstate highways, excluding the interstate system.

headings.title: Emergency utility response permits after disasters and rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Requires issuing emergency utility response permits (including verbal approval in exigent circumstances) for post-disaster utility repair transport at any time/day, with chapter 536 nonseverability rulemaking.

headings.title: Eighty-six-thousand-pound interstate weight limits for fire vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Permits emergency fire-suppression/hazmat vehicles up to 86,000 pounds gross weight (with specific steering, drive, and tandem axle caps) solely on the interstate highway system.

headings.title: Eighty-two-thousand-pound gross weight allowance for natural gas vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Permits natural-gas-fueled vehicles to exceed weight limits by the tank/fuel-system weight difference over comparable diesel systems, up to 82,000 pounds gross weight.

headings.title: Weight limits for local log trucks and local log truck tractors
headings.reviewNote: Permits local log trucks up to 22,400 lbs single axle, 44,800 lbs tandem axle, 15,000 lbs/GVWR front axle, and 109,600 lbs gross weight, excluding interstates and extended-distance permit travel outside radius.
